Report the Seller (But Do It Properly)** - **How?** - Go to the seller’s listing → Click **"Report this listing"** → Select **"Suspicious activity"** or **"Review manipulation"** (Amazon’s exact wording may vary). - If you can’t find the exact option, use the **"Contact Seller"** link and explain: > *"I received a free item in exchange for a review I did not leave. This violates Amazon’s review policies. Please investigate this seller for review manipulation."* - **Why?** This gives Amazon direct evidence of their violation. #### **2. Leave a Neutral or Negative Review (If You Haven’t Already)** - Since you didn’t actually leave a review, you can now **leave a truthful but critical review** (e.g., *"Received a free item without leaving a review—this is against Amazon’s policies."*). - This adds **public pressure** and makes it harder for them to continue the practice. #### **3. Report the Hotmail Address to Amazon (If Possible)** - If you can find the Hotmail address they used, you can report it as part of the seller’s **contact information** (via Seller Central or Amazon’s feedback system). - This may help Amazon track their review-buying scheme. #### **4. Consider Reporting to the FTC (If You Want to Go Further)** - If this seller has a pattern of fake reviews (which they likely do), you could file a complaint with the **Federal Trade Commission (FTC)** at [reportfraud.ftc.gov](https://reportfraud.ftc.gov/). While Amazon is the primary target here, the FTC may investigate if this is part of a larger scam. #### **5. Warn Other Buyers (Anonymously)** - If you’re comfortable, you could leave a **warning in the comments section** of their listings (e.g., *"This seller offers free items for reviews—don’t fall for it!"*). - This doesn’t violate Amazon’s rules but helps others avoid the same issue. --- ### **Why Not Just Ignore It?** - **They’re Likely Doing It to Many Others** – If they’ve been doing this for years with 100% ratings, they’ve probably manipulated thousands of reviews. Reporting helps Amazon catch them. - **Amazon’s Algorithms Are Getting Smarter** – If enough buyers report them, Amazon may **suspend their account**, which would hurt their business. - **You Got a Free Item—But at What Cost?** – While you benefited once, you’re supporting a seller who **misleads customers**, which can lead to **higher prices for everyone** (since fake reviews make their products seem more popular than they are). --- ### **Final Verdict: Yes, You Should Report Them** But **don’t just report them—take a multi-step approach** to maximize the impact.
